checked_sources: independent reconstruction of both 64-vertex conflict graphs and exact independent-set optima
correctness.rationale: The channel definitions were reconstructed directly. An independent exact conflict-graph computation on all \(64\) length-six words gives \(56\) duplication-conflict edges and \(34\) deletion-conflict edges. Exact maximum-independent-set optimization returns \(40\) and \(42\), respectively. The package certificates independently realize the same bounds: a 40-word duplication packing plus 24 disjoint conflict edges, and a 42-word deletion packing plus a disjoint partition into eight conflict triangles, six conflict edges, and 28 singletons. These upper certificates are logically sufficient without relying on an optimizer.

value.rationale: The exact parameter is not arbitrary: it is the very binary length-six, block-length-two setting used in the foundational paper to demonstrate nonequivalence of palindromic duplication and deletion correction. Replacing witness-level nonequivalence by the exact extremal separation \(40<42\) gives a motivated quantitative answer and a reusable benchmark for this error model.
residual_risks: The contribution is a single finite benchmark rather than a general formula.

final_claim: For binary source words of length \(6\), one palindromic duplication of block length \(2\) has exact correcting-code optimum \(40\), while one palindromic deletion of block length \(2\) has exact optimum \(42\).
limitations: Only the binary alphabet, source length \(6\), block length \(2\), and one error are covered.
The result determines the two optimum cardinalities but does not classify all optimal codes or give an asymptotic theorem.
